claims.text: A Cr coating on zirconium alloy can be modified by co-sputtering approximately 1–2 at.% Si.
Thermal exposure of the Si-modified Cr coating will form a CrSi2 interlayer at the Cr/Zr-alloy interface.
The resulting CrSi2 interlayer will be continuous and coherent.
A controlled post-deposition thermal treatment can promote formation of the proposed interfacial CrSi2 layer without compromising the Cr coating.
CrSi2 has intrinsically low atomic diffusivity.
The CrSi2 interlayer interrupts fast atomic-diffusion paths along coating grain boundaries and across the Cr/Zr interface.
Interrupting these diffusion paths will significantly inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion contributes to premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
The proposed silicide barrier will remain effective in subcritical water at approximately 320 °C.
The proposed silicide barrier will remain effective during steam exposure at approximately 1150–1200 °C for 1–2 hours.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Si-modified coating will have a lower Cr–Zr interdiffusion-zone depth and interdiffusion rate.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will extend the coating's protective lifetime and improve long-term stability.
The Si-modified coating will preserve oxidation protection under both normal-operation water and accident-relevant steam conditions.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating lacks a silicide interlayer and is more susceptible to rapid Cr–Zr interdiffusion in high-temperature steam.
As-deposited coatings of the type considered have a fine-grained microstructure.
Uniform and continuous CrSi2 formation over complex cladding geometries is uncertain.
The post-deposition treatment temperature and duration require optimization.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction, exemplified as more than a 30% decrease in interdiffusion-zone thickness, or failure to form continuous CrSi2 will falsify the hypothesis.
